Current: Premium limit set by IRS (indexed; $200,000 after SECURE 2.0). Excluded from required minimum distributions until payments start.
Proposed: Premium limit set by IRS and indexed for inflation ($210,000 for 2025 and 2026, up from $200,000 set by SECURE 2.0). Excluded from required minimum distributions until payments start.
Reason: The $200,000 figure is out of date; IRS Notice 2025-67 keeps the QLAC limit at $210,000 for 2026.

Current: Oregon requires it for lawyers (through the Oregon State Bar PLF); most states require disclosure of whether lawyers carry it.
Proposed: Only Oregon (through the Oregon State Bar PLF, since 1978) and Idaho (since 2018) require private-practice lawyers to carry it. About half the states require lawyers to disclose whether they carry it, either to clients or on bar registration forms.
Reason: Idaho has required malpractice cover since 1 Jan 2018, so Oregon is not the only state. 'Most states require disclosure' overstates it: the ABA counts roughly 7 states with direct client disclosure and about 18 with registration disclosure (about 25, i.e. about half).

Current: Package policy for homes that combines cover for the dwelling, other structures, belongings, loss of use (extra living costs) and personal liability. Standard ISO forms are numbered HO-1 to HO-8.
Proposed: Package policy for homes that combines cover for the dwelling, other structures, belongings, loss of use (extra living costs) and personal liability. The current ISO homeowners forms are HO-2, HO-3, HO-4, HO-5, HO-6 and HO-8; HO-1 has been withdrawn in nearly all states, and 'HO-7' is an industry label for mobile home cover, not an ISO form.
Reason: ISO has no HO-7 form (mobile homes are written with endorsement MH 04 01 attached to HO-2 or HO-3), and the HO-1 form has been withdrawn in nearly all states, so 'standard ISO forms numbered HO-1 to HO-8' is inaccurate.

Current: Required by dram shop laws in many states; CGL excludes it for businesses selling alcohol.
Proposed: Dram shop laws in many states make businesses that serve alcohol liable for harm caused by intoxicated customers, and some states (e.g. Minnesota) require liquor licensees to prove liability cover. The CGL excludes this risk for businesses that make, sell or serve alcohol.
Reason: Dram shop laws create liability; they do not themselves require insurance. The insurance requirement comes from separate licensing laws in some states (e.g. Minn. Stat. 340A.409).

Current: Sold on HealthCare.gov or a state-run exchange (e.g. Covered California). Premium tax credits available on-exchange by income. Open enrollment runs each fall.
Proposed: Sold on HealthCare.gov or a state-run exchange (e.g. Covered California). Premium tax credits are available on-exchange by income; the temporary 'enhanced' credits expired at the end of 2025, so from 2026 households above 400% of the federal poverty level again get no credit. Open enrollment starts Nov 1 each year (HealthCare.gov runs to Jan 15; state exchange dates vary).
Reason: Omits the 2026 return of the 400% FPL subsidy cliff after the enhanced credits expired; 'runs each fall' is imprecise because HealthCare.gov open enrollment runs to Jan 15.

Current: Federal duration limits have changed several times (2018 and 2024 rules; check current federal status). Some states restrict or ban it outright.
Proposed: A 2024 federal rule limited STLDI to 3 months (4 months with renewals), but in August 2025 the federal agencies said they would not enforce those limits while they write a new rule. Some states restrict or ban it outright.
Reason: The current note tells readers to 'check current federal status' instead of giving it; the 7 Aug 2025 non-enforcement statement is the current federal position.

Current: Contribution limits set yearly by the IRS; triple tax advantage.
Proposed: Contribution limits set yearly by the IRS; triple tax advantage. From 2026, all bronze and catastrophic plans count as HSA-eligible, and people with certain direct primary care arrangements can contribute (One Big Beautiful Bill Act; IRS Notice 2026-5).
Reason: Leaves out the 2026 federal change that widened HSA eligibility.

Current: Not eligible for premium tax credits.
Proposed: Not eligible for premium tax credits. Treated as HSA-eligible from 2026.
Reason: Leaves out the 2026 change that made catastrophic (and bronze) plans HSA-compatible.

Current: Each state runs its own program within federal rules; 40 states plus DC have expanded Medicaid under the ACA to adults up to 138% of the federal poverty level. Most enrollees are in private managed care plans contracted by the state.
Proposed: Each state runs its own program within federal rules; 40 states plus DC have expanded Medicaid under the ACA to adults up to 138% of the federal poverty level. Most enrollees are in private managed care plans contracted by the state. Under the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, expansion adults face work/community-engagement requirements (80 hours a month) and 6-month eligibility renewals starting by Dec 31, 2026.
Reason: Leaves out major federal changes that take effect at the end of 2026. The expansion count (41 including DC) is still correct per KFF.

Current: The most common individual life product sold in the US by policy count.
Proposed: One of the most widely bought individual life products and the cheapest per dollar of cover; whole life and indexed UL now bring in more new premium.
Reason: 'Most common by policy count' has no source. LIMRA reports whole life (37%) and IUL (25%) ahead of term (17%) on new premium in 2025, and whole life policy counts grew faster.

Current: Cash value earns interest linked to a stock market index (e.g. the S&P 500), subject to a cap and a floor (often 0%), so it doesn't lose value from market drops.
Proposed: Cash value earns interest linked to a stock market index (e.g. the S&P 500), subject to a cap and a floor (often 0%). The floor stops index losses, but policy charges and cost of insurance can still reduce the cash value.
Reason: Saying it 'doesn't lose value from market drops' is misleading: monthly charges come out even in 0% years, so cash value can fall.

Current: HO-7 Mobile Home Form
Proposed: Mobile / Manufactured Home Insurance
Reason: 'HO-7' is not an ISO form (ISO uses endorsement MH 04 01 on HO-2/HO-3). Presenting it as a standard form misleads learners. Keep 'HO-7' as an Also Known As label.

Current: Manufactured home insurance
Proposed: Manufactured home insurance; HO-7 (non-ISO label)
Reason: Goes with the name change above.

Current: Group Life & Employee Benefits
Proposed: Group & Business Life Insurance
Reason: Key person, buy-sell, COLI and split-dollar are individually underwritten policies owned by businesses, not group life. Either rename the parent (this row) or move rows 44-47 to a new 'Business-Owned Life Insurance' node under Life.
Source URL: (reasoning: product structure; see IRC 101(j) for employer-owned individual policies) https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/101

Current: life.group_life
Proposed: life.business_life (new level-2 node 'Business-Owned Life Insurance'), or keep under renamed life.group_life
Reason: This is an individual policy owned by a business, not group life (alternative to renaming the parent).

Current: life.group_life
Proposed: life.business_life (new level-2 node 'Business-Owned Life Insurance'), or keep under renamed life.group_life
Reason: This is an individual policy owned by a business, not group life (alternative to renaming the parent).

Current: life.group_life
Proposed: life.business_life (new level-2 node 'Business-Owned Life Insurance'), or keep under renamed life.group_life
Reason: This is an individual policy owned by a business, not group life (alternative to renaming the parent).

Current: life.group_life
Proposed: life.business_life (new level-2 node 'Business-Owned Life Insurance'), or keep under renamed life.group_life
Reason: This is an individual policy owned by a business, not group life (alternative to renaming the parent).

Current: health.disability
Proposed: health.supplemental (next to Accident Insurance) or life.group_life
Reason: AD&D pays for accidental death or loss of a limb. It is an accident/life product, not income replacement for disability, and the row itself says it is 'often bundled with group life'.

Current: Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract (QLAC)
Proposed: Qualifying Longevity Annuity Contract (QLAC)
Reason: The IRS regulation (Treas. Reg. 1.401(a)(9)-6(q)) uses 'qualifying', not 'qualified'.

Current: Inflation Reduction Act capped Part D out-of-pocket spending at $2,000 in 2025 (indexed after).
Proposed: The Inflation Reduction Act capped Part D out-of-pocket drug spending at $2,000 in 2025; the cap is indexed and is $2,100 in 2026.
Reason: Add the current-year figure.

Current: Now covers roughly half of Medicare beneficiaries. Annual enrollment Oct 15-Dec 7.
Proposed: Covers more than half of eligible Medicare beneficiaries (54% in 2025). Annual Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15-Dec 7.
Reason: 'Roughly half' understates it; KFF puts 2025 enrollment at 54%.

Current: Closed to people newly eligible for Medicare on or after Jan 1, 2020 (MACRA).
Proposed: Plans C and F are closed to people newly eligible for Medicare on or after Jan 1, 2020 (MACRA), because new plans can no longer cover the Part B deductible.
Reason: Plan C is closed by the same rule; add it for completeness.

Current: About 30+ states plus DC have FAIR plans; usually named-peril cover that may need a separate "difference in conditions" policy.
Proposed: About 33 states plus DC have FAIR plans; usually named-peril cover that may need a separate 'difference in conditions' policy.
Reason: Give the more precise count reported by the Insurance Information Institute.

Current: Covers damage from earthquakes, typically with a deductible of 10-25% of the dwelling limit.
Proposed: Covers damage from earthquakes, typically with a deductible of 5-25% of the dwelling limit.
Reason: The California Earthquake Authority offers 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% deductibles.

Current: Premiums set by FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 method; usually a 30-day waiting period. Program requires periodic reauthorization by Congress.
Proposed: Premiums set by FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 method; usually a 30-day waiting period. The program needs periodic reauthorization by Congress (most recently extended to Dec 11, 2026); if it lapses, FEMA pays claims but cannot sell or renew policies.
Reason: Adds the current deadline and what a lapse means. Dates change often, so review this regularly.

Current: Examples: SCIF (California), NYSIF (New York), Texas Mutual.
Proposed: Examples: SCIF (California), NYSIF (New York), Texas Mutual (created by the Texas legislature and now a private mutual that acts as the state's insurer of last resort).
Reason: Texas Mutual has not been a state fund since 2001; it is a domestic mutual and not a state agency.

Current: Temporary disability programs exist in CA, HI, NJ, NY, RI and PR. A growing number of states (e.g. WA, MA, CT, OR, CO, MD, MN, DE, ME) have paid family and medical leave programs.
Proposed: Temporary disability programs exist in CA, HI, NJ, NY, RI and PR. Paid family and medical leave programs pay benefits in CA, NJ, NY, RI, WA, MA, CT, OR, CO, MN, DE, ME and DC; Maryland's benefits are delayed to 2028.
Reason: Maryland is not paying benefits yet; MN and DE started in Jan 2026 and ME in May 2026.

Current: Popular for estate planning; reserves governed by NAIC Actuarial Guideline 38 (AXXX).
Proposed: Popular for estate planning. Reserves for older policies follow NAIC Actuarial Guideline 38 (AXXX); policies issued from 2020 use principles-based reserving (VM-20).
Reason: AG 38 no longer governs new-business reserves since VM-20 became mandatory on 1 Jan 2020.

Current: Created by federal rule in 2020.
Proposed: Created by a 2019 federal rule, available from Jan 1, 2020.
Reason: The rule was finalized in June 2019 and took effect for plan years from 2020.

Current: SCO was created by the 2014 Farm Bill; ECO added by RMA in 2021.
Proposed: SCO was created by the 2014 Farm Bill; ECO added by RMA in 2021. From the 2026 crop year the premium subsidy for SCO and ECO rose to 80% (One Big Beautiful Bill Act).
Reason: Adds the 2026 subsidy change.

Current: Interest is linked to a market index with a cap and a zero floor, so principal isn't lost to market drops.
Proposed: Interest is linked to a market index with a cap and a zero floor, so principal isn't lost to market drops (though surrender charges and rider fees can reduce what you get back if you withdraw early).
Reason: Adds a caveat so the no-loss claim isn't overstated.

Current: Personal Property Insurance
Proposed: Home & Personal Property Insurance
Reason: In insurance, 'personal property' means belongings (Coverage C), so a branch named 'Personal Property Insurance' that covers dwellings will confuse learners.
